body.x: Autonomous driving, software-defined vehicles and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) move large volumes of sensor data through a car, and the wiring that carries it has to be light, fast and resistant to electromagnetic interference (EMI).
Fiber optics offer one route, and KD builds the chips for it.

KD (Knowledge Development for POF, S.L.), a semiconductor company headquartered in Madrid, designs integrated circuits for high-speed optical connectivity in automotive, industrial and home networking applications. Led by CEO Carlos Pardo, KD is taking part in KES 2026 with its automotive solution, the KD7251, and related hardware.

According to the company, the KD7251 and its supporting hardware enable lightweight, high-speed in-vehicle communication for autonomous driving, software-defined vehicles, ADAS and high-resolution sensor connections. KD says its products are designed to deliver low latency and immunity to EMI while carrying multi-gigabit data over optical fiber.

KD says it has been adopted by OEMs worldwide as a multi-gigabit network solution and has secured about 10 mass-production projects. It contributes to international connectivity standards and works with global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. The company is running proof-of-concept projects and business discussions with automotive OEMs around the world and has offices in Korea, Taiwan, Germany and the United States.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
